name: Congenital Velopharyngeal Incompetence

criteria.description: Presence of audible nasal air emission during speech
Hypernasality of speech confirmed by speech pathology evaluation
Demonstrated failure of velopharyngeal closure on nasoendoscopy or videofluoroscopy
No evidence of overt cleft palate or submucous cleft
Speech delay or articulation disorder secondary to velopharyngeal dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypernasal speech and nasal air emission with confirmed velopharyngeal closure failure on imaging or endoscopy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of structural cleft palate and other causes of velopharyngeal dysfunction.

imaging: Videofluoroscopic swallow study showing velopharyngeal insufficiency
genetic: Possible association with syndromes involving 22q11.2 deletion (DiGeorge syndrome)
No single causative gene identified for isolated cases
other: Speech pathology evaluation confirming hypernasality and articulation errors
Audiological assessment for middle ear function

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of bifid uvula or zona pellucida on palate exam
Often associated with overt palatal structural abnormalities
Structural defects of the palate visible on exam or imaging
More severe velopharyngeal gap on imaging

redFlags: Persistent severe hypernasality despite speech therapy
Recurrent otitis media with hearing loss
Signs of syndromic association (e.g., cardiac anomalies, facial dysmorphism)
references: Kummer AW. Velopharyngeal Dysfunction: Diagnosis and Management. 3rd ed. Plural Publishing; 2016.
Sell D, Harding-Bell A, et al. Velopharyngeal insufficiency: diagnosis and management. Arch Dis Child. 2015;100(12):1163-1168.
